distinguishing_features: A physical high-conductivity metallic annular cap/spreader integrated at the ceramic-metal seal interface rather than a software thermal-stress indicator and derating control.
Passive reduction of interface thermal time constant and local temperature nonuniformity by conduction spreading.
Thermal-contact treatment or metallization/paste at the ceramic-spreader interface to reduce contact resistance.
Use of the spreader in place of a thick compliant interlayer while retaining only a thin assembly adhesive.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce crack initiation in a ceramic-metal seal during thermal cycling caused by differential thermal expansion.
parsed.viable_reason: A heat spreader may smooth local gradients, but it does not reduce the steady CTE-mismatch strain produced by a 225 K uniform temperature rise, so the stated crack-prevention mechanism cannot by itself keep stress below threshold.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 2 already teaches that reducing peak thermal excursions and ΔT reduces thermal-fatigue cracking, and using a conventional high-conductivity spreader/contact treatment for that purpose is routine.
